alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines require creatinine (eGFR) monitoring for TDF at 3 months, 6 months, and then 6-12 monthly. The patient is on TDF and has hypertension, a known risk factor for renal impairment. The current plan does not include scheduling the next creatinine test. While the latest creatinine of 112 umol/L is within normal limits, regular monitoring is mandated to detect early renal changes.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule next creatinine (eGFR) test as per 6-12 monthly monitoring guideline for TDF.

alerts.title: TDF use with hypertension risk
alerts.message: Guidelines advise caution with TDF in high-risk patients, particularly those with co-existent hypertension. This patient has hypertension (BP 146/94) and trace proteinuria, indicating possible renal stress. TDF is associated with renal failure and tubular wasting syndrome. The combination of TDF, hypertension, and NSAID use (ibuprofen) compounds renal risk. Non-drug causes like hypertension itself can contribute to proteinuria.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor renal function closely; consider TAF if renal function declines or hypertension remains uncontrolled.

alerts.title: NSAID use with TDF and hypertension
alerts.message: The patient uses ibuprofen as needed for back pain. Ibuprofen is an NSAID which can impair renal function, especially in the context of dehydration or intercurrent illness. Guidelines highlight that intercurrent illnesses with dehydration may cause renal deterioration in patients on TDF. Concurrent use of TDF, hypertension, and an NSAID increases the risk of acute kidney injury. The plan does not address this interaction or provide safer pain management alternatives.

evidence.recommended_action: Advise against regular/prn ibuprofen; recommend non-NSAID analgesics and stress hydration, especially during travel.

alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypertension plan
alerts.message: Blood pressure is suboptimally controlled at 146/94 mmHg, and the patient admits to missing amlodipine doses. The plan only refills amlodipine without addressing adherence barriers or considering intensification. Guidelines note amlodipine can cause lower limb edema. The patient has no edema reported, but uncontrolled hypertension increases cardiovascular and renal risk, especially alongside TDF and proteinuria.

evidence.recommended_action: Address antihypertensive adherence; consider dose adjustment or addition of a second agent per hypertension guidelines.

alerts.title: CD4 monitoring may be optional
alerts.message: Guidelines state CD4 monitoring can be stopped if CD4+ > 200 cells/µL and the patient is virologically suppressed. This patient's CD4 is 540 cells/µL and viral load is <50 copies/mL. Continuing 6-monthly CD4 testing may not be required, allowing resources to be focused on other monitoring like renal function.

evidence.recommended_action: Consider stopping routine CD4 monitoring as per guideline, focusing on viral load and renal monitoring.
